Request-lexicon FALSE POSITIVES override the model’s explicit non-mutation classification. With requestIntent.kind = other (the class the prompt assigns to drafting/conversational turns), a lexicon verb or verb-noun anywhere in the command derives intent and the truthful reply is replaced by the receipt: drafting 20/20 (‘draft an email to Bob about the merge’, ‘write a memo on fire safety at ACME’, ‘brainstorm names for the new hire’), conversational statements 17/20 (‘the fire drill is at 3pm’, ‘I approve of this plan’, ‘the revenue split is 60/40’, ‘the store will reopen Monday’), noun-phrase reads 7/15 (‘history of the ACME archive’). Only kind = read vetoes the lexicon (0/55 then). OTM §3 rule 2: text shape is the sole reason a truthful reply is rewritten. Prepared fix F1: other vetoes the lexicon like read (the lexicon acts only when the model gave no classification).

The command-derived company fallback ignores requestIntent.entityType: ‘archive Alpha’ with the model classifying {kind: mutation, entityType: task|person|goal|project, targetName: Alpha} and emitting no field archives the COMPANY Alpha (exact name) with the receipt ‘Alpha: archived.’ (no entity type). The gate’s own comment claims this check; the code lacks it. Realistic via company/project name collisions. Prepared fix F2.

Negations/hypotheticals with a lexicon verb and no read shape get the receipt with a misleading reason (‘don’t archive ACME’ -> ‘No change was made — I could not resolve which company you meant’); the lifecycle commandIsQuestion lacks the POLITE_REQUEST exemption (a polite question with the model emitting nothing is refused, never executed); a compound command with the model emitting nothing executes only the first clause and drops the second silently (‘archive Alpha and restore Beta’ -> ‘Alpha: archived.’); a model field in the opposite direction to the command executes the model’s direction; 1-char company names cannot be resolved by name.
